title: Smart Access & Monitoring System — SAMS
summary: An 8051 access-control and environmental-monitoring design combining PIN authentication, sensor inputs, event logging and emergency override.
overview: SAMS brings access control and environmental monitoring into one 8051 academic design. Its scope includes multi-level PIN authentication, temperature and light sensing, an interrupt-driven emergency override and event logging. The project is documented through a Proteus circuit schematic; physical implementation remains unverified.
approach: Defined multi-level PIN authentication through a 4×3 keypad, with LCD/LED feedback and a relay interface for door control.
Included LM35 temperature and LDR light inputs in the monitoring architecture.
Specified an interrupt-driven emergency override and hardware-timer use alongside the normal access and monitoring functions.
Included FIFO/circular-buffer event logging in the software scope and brought the controller, keypad, sensing, feedback and relay connections together in Proteus.
components: Interrupts, hardware timers and circular-buffer logging
outcomes: Documented the proposed circuit integration in Proteus, including keypad, LCD, sensor and relay interfaces.
Established the academic scope for authentication, interrupts, timers and buffered event logging. Hardware implementation is not confirmed in the available record.

evidenceNotes: Only a Proteus schematic was found; no physical photograph or additional implementation evidence.
problem: Bring access decisions and environmental monitoring into one controller design while retaining an emergency override and a record of events.
context: An 8051 academic access-control and monitoring design. The supplied evidence is a Proteus schematic; a physical hardware build remains unverified.
constraints: Authentication, sensing and feedback share the controller, while the emergency input requires a distinct interrupt-driven response.
The schematic establishes circuit-design evidence; it does not establish physical installation, measured sensor performance or deployed access security.
lessons: Access control and monitoring involve more than a PIN check: emergency response, user feedback and event handling also shape the controller design.
nextSteps: Further development would require a documented physical implementation and validation of access, sensor, logging and emergency-override behaviour.
